R3-01.why: Strongest premise in the set: 'Mom's home, hide the mess' is universally relatable and readable with no context. The thumbnail sells itself: an angry parent in the doorway, a trashed living room, a kid stuffing the TV into the oven, and it matches the actual gameplay. All three viral drivers are present: chaos (party smashing), fear (Granny-style parent hunt, the FREEZE! snapshot catching someone mid-sneak) and betrayal (Snitch). Each round has a built-in arc and punchline (party, then panic, then hunt, then Report Card 'Most Ridiculous Hiding Spot'), which fits a 15-60 s short. The parent role suits creators (one streamer as Mom vs their audience). Weaknesses: for 1:45 of each round the Parent is in a separate lane-dodge driving mini-game. That is the least clip-worthy footage in the game, and it pulls the creator-as-Parent out of the chaos they are meant to react to. PANIC switches to an elevated tap-to-hide camera, which reads less like slapstick than physical scrambling. Crude humour is avoided, so takedown risk is low.
R3-01.fix: Make the drive a short picture-in-picture or a ring-doorbell feed the kids can see ('Mom is 30 s away!'), or let the Parent watch the party through a 'nanny cam' they can tap to mark rooms. Keep the Parent's face/reaction on screen during the party. Keep a physical third-person scramble during PANIC (the elevated camera only as a toggle). Add a 'Mom's view' kill-cam replay when FREEZE! catches someone.

R3-02.why: Has some clip moments: a misfire that turns lightning into a rubber chicken, a friend launched off the balcony by a Firenado, screen-filling named fusion banners, and finger-drawing on a phone is a format that films well. But it is co-op PvE wave defence from fixed balconies with no camera control. That footage looks like many tower-defence and magic games, and it has no fear or betrayal tension. Run-to-run variety is mostly relic-build depth, which is fun to play but not to show friends. The thumbnail (wizard plus a big fire tornado) is generic fantasy and does not show the unique hook (drawing) unless you add a hand/finger overlay. Viewers with no context see effects, not a situation.
R3-02.fix: Put friendship stakes into the core. Make misfires more frequent and more consequential (a misfire hits a teammate or summons a monster). Add a 'blame the scribbler' replay showing the ugly drawing beside the disaster. Consider a versus or traitor mode (one apprentice secretly sabotages fusions). Make the thumbnail a giant crude doodle on screen turning into a disaster.

R3-03.why: Red-Light-Green-Light tension plus hide-in-plain-sight is a proven creator format (Squid Game clips, Be NPC or Die). The flashlight sweep creates natural near-misses ('he looked right at me'). The pranks are visual, harmless gags that read in one frame (a moustache on the portrait, the knight's helmet on the T-rex) and keep it clean. The Night at the Museum premise and a guard's beam on a frozen statue in a dark gallery make a clear thumbnail that matches gameplay. The Unmasking reveal is a good payoff, and streamer-as-Guard vs audience works. Limits: the genre is crowded (DISGUISE, In Plain Sight, Be NPC or Die), so clips feel familiar. There is no betrayal mechanic. Auto-snap plinth poses remove the funny-pose comedy that drives hide-in-plain-sight clips. Most of the tension is quiet, slow standing-still, which needs commentary to land.
R3-03.fix: Let players freeze in whatever ridiculous pose they are caught in (or choose from silly poses), and reveal those at the Unmasking. Add a betrayal lever: a statue can 'point' at another statue to frame them, or a secret Guard-informant statue. Add a 'Caught on Camera' video replay of the near-miss (beam passing within inches), not just stills.

R3-04.why: Coordination-chaos games (Chained Together, RV There Yet?, Fart Together) are a top creator genre, and the 'WHO SANK US?' blame card plus the slow-mo waterfall freeze-frame naming a guilty player are genuinely shareable. The Saboteur Seat adds betrayal, and the thumbnail (six friends in a bathtub going over a waterfall) is clear and matches gameplay. However, the cited evidence cuts both ways: the crude version took off, and the clean version (Boat Together) peaked around 2K. Much of the comedy in this genre comes from creators shouting at each other on voice, not from what the game shows on screen. A server-kinematic raft on a spline, with seated hold-to-paddle and no thumbstick, removes the unpredictable physics, the ragdolls and the people falling overboard that produce unexpected outcomes. Footage of people holding buttons on a boat is low-energy without the voice track.
R3-04.fix: Make the Saboteur Seat a standard mode, not a weekly mutator (a 'one paddler is a traitor' variant), since betrayal is the big clip driver here. Add cosmetic ragdoll ejections (players flung overboard and swimming back, client-side, with no gameplay physics). Bring a signature non-crude gag to the vehicles (the sneezing walrus works if it is loud and frequent). Overlay each seat's input timeline on the replay so the blame reads without voice.

R3-05.why: A burning house with a puppy to save makes a clear, emotional thumbnail that matches gameplay, and there are some funny failures (a goat eats the hose, an elephant sprays the team) and last-second saves as the floor collapses, which make decent clips. But it is wholesome co-op with no betrayal and only mild fear, so the moments are 'satisfying' rather than 'you have to see this'. The collection loop leans toward grind and checklists, which don't make good clips. Footage of an Overcooked-style firefighting session needs commentary to be funny, and many fire sims already exist, so the visuals are not distinctive. The strongest comedy (critter mayhem) is a side event, not the core.
R3-05.fix: Make critter chaos the headline, not a side effect: every building has a 'problem critter' (a flaming-tail fox spreading fire, a hose-chewing goat) that the team must wrangle. Add a friendly-fire hose (blasting a teammate out of a window) and a 'Hero Cam' replay of the save of the round. Add a light betrayal or credit-stealing element (snatching the rescued critter at the door to claim the collection credit).

overall_notes: Ranking: R3-01 > R3-03 > R3-04 > R3-02 = R3-05. Only R3-01 combines all three clip drivers (chaos, fear, betrayal) with a no-context premise anyone gets in one second. Its main risk is the Parent's off-screen driving phase. R3-03 has strong tension and visual pranks but sits in a crowded genre and lacks betrayal. R3-04 depends on voice-chat chemistry and its clean predecessor underperformed, so promote the Saboteur Seat. R3-02 and R3-05 are pleasant co-op PvE with good spectacle but few 'show your friends' situations. None of the five relies on crude humour, so takedown risk is low across the board.
